title: Vector and Echo
premise: Zephyrine Dunmore investigates a manifest anomaly aboard the Meridian Vale, a freighter officially destroyed eleven years ago, and discovers her dead mother's name among its crew. The ship is a ghost maintained by two rival fleets who each believe the other destroyed it, and the fragile truce between them rests on that lie. As Zephyrine traces the manifest through smuggler stations and black-box recordings, she learns her mother faked the disaster to prevent a war, sacrificing her own name and crew's reputations to do it. With the jump window closing and both fleets mobilizing, Zephyrine must choose between exposing the truth that would exonerate her mother and preserve the lie that keeps the peace — ultimately broadcasting a partial truth that honors the dead without igniting the war they died to stop.
about_author: Silas Villalobos is a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent a decade reconstructing accidents no one wanted explained. He writes from a converted tugboat off the Pacific coast, where he keeps an archive of unsolved manifests.

chapters.title: The Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Zephyrine Dunmore, investigating impossible-accident claims for Halcyon Mutual, flags a cargo manifest listing the Meridian Vale — a vessel officially lost with all hands eleven years ago. Her supervisor dismisses it as clerical error. POV: Zephyrine. Beat: quiet unease; the professional instinct that something is wrong before anyone else sees it.

chapters.title: An Unfamiliar Name
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing crew records, Zephyrine finds a name she doesn't recognize on the ghost ship's roster — yet the handwriting in the digital signature matches her mother's, dead these nine years. She requests the original claim file and finds it sealed by military order. POV: Zephyrine. Beat: grief rekindled into obsession; the personal hooking into the professional.

chapters.title: Sealed by Order
chapters.summary: Zephyrine pressures a retired claims adjuster, Odile Ferrant, who processed the original loss. Odile warns her to drop it: 'Some files are closed because opening them kills people.' That night Zephyrine's apartment is searched. POV: Zephyrine. Beat: first threat; the stakes turn from curiosity to danger.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Grave
chapters.summary: Zephyrine learns the Meridian Vale's destruction is the founding grievance of the Concord fleet and the Free Anchor flotilla, whose cold war has frozen the jump lanes for a decade. Each blames the other; the wreck site sits in neutral space neither will enter. POV: Zephyrine. Beat: scale expands — one ship, one war's worth of grief.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Denied leave, Zephyrine resigns and books passage on a slow hauler along the smuggling circuit toward neutral space. Aboard, she meets Toma Reyes, a disgraced Concord navigator who recognizes her surname and flinches. POV: Zephyrine. Beat: commitment; leaving the lawful world behind.

chapters.title: What Toma Saw
chapters.summary: Toma confesses he was a junior officer the night of the disaster and saw sensor data that never made official reports — the Meridian Vale jumped under its own power after the explosion was logged. POV: Toma. Beat: the first crack in the official story; guilt as motive.

chapters.title: Hollow Station
chapters.summary: At a smuggler station in the drift, Zephyrine buys access to a black-market archive and finds maintenance logs proving the Meridian Vale has been secretly serviced for years — someone is keeping the ghost alive. POV: Zephyrine. Beat: wonder curdling into dread; the accident may be ongoing.

chapters.title: The Keeper
chapters.summary: Following the maintenance trail, Zephyrine locates the ship itself, hidden in a debris shoal, tended by an old engineer named Brannoch — her mother's chief mechanic, who has kept her flying for eleven years. POV: Zephyrine. Beat: awe and heartbreak; the dead ship breathing.

chapters.title: Mother's Voice
chapters.summary: Brannoch plays Zephyrine a recording her mother left: Captain Ilsa Dunmore deliberately staged the destruction, with her crew's consent, to give both fleets a shared martyr rather than a casus belli. The unfamiliar name on the manifest is Ilsa's alias. POV: flashback within Zephyrine's frame. Beat: devastating revelation; inheritance reframed as burden.

chapters.title: Why She Lied
chapters.summary: The recording continues: intelligence showed both fleets maneuvering toward open war over a navigation dispute; only a tragedy blamed on neither side could freeze them. Ilsa asks whoever finds this to keep the lie — or end it cleanly, never half. POV: flashback. Beat: moral weight transferred; the mother's choice becomes the daughter's.

chapters.title: Concord Comes Calling
chapters.summary: A Concord patrol stumbles onto the shoal. Toma negotiates their escape using his old codes, but the patrol reports the sighting. Both fleets now know the Meridian Vale exists. POV: Toma. Beat: point of no return; the secret is loose.

chapters.title: The Race for the Wreck
chapters.summary: Zephyrine, Toma, and Brannoch must reach the jump gate before either fleet seizes the ship and its proof. En route they're boarded by Free Anchor privateers led by Captain Sefa Okonkwo, who lost family in the disaster. POV: Zephyrine. Beat: pursuit tension; grief on all sides.

chapters.title: Sefa's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sefa shows Zephyrine the Free Anchor casualty list — including Sefa's brother, listed as Meridian Vale crew. Zephyrine realizes her mother's crew included volunteers from both fleets, chosen so every faction would mourn. POV: Sefa. Beat: empathy across enemy lines; the lie's human cost made intimate.

chapters.title: Mutiny of Grief
chapters.summary: Sefa's crew demands the ship be handed to Free Anchor as proof of Concord treachery. Toma argues the reverse. Zephyrine, holding the recording, realizes truth in either hand becomes a weapon. POV: Zephyrine. Beat: loyalty vs. truth crystallized; allies fracture.

chapters.title: The Jump Window
chapters.summary: Astrogation confirms the neutral-space jump window — the only route both fleets can reach simultaneously — closes in forty hours. Whoever controls the narrative at the gate controls the peace or the war. Both fleets race there. POV: Toma. Beat: ticking clock engaged; geography becomes destiny.

chapters.title: Broadcast Interception
chapters.summary: Zephyrine intercepts fleet communications: Concord plans to display the ship as evidence of Free Anchor sabotage; Free Anchor plans the mirror image. Brannoch reveals Ilsa left him a second message, sealed, 'for when the lie starts killing.' POV: Zephyrine. Beat: dread deepens; the mother anticipated this moment.

chapters.title: The Second Message
chapters.summary: The sealed message contains full sensor logs exonerating both fleets — and naming Ilsa as saboteur of her own ship, a confession that would disgrace her but dissolve the war's pretext. Ilsa trusted her daughter to decide which truth the galaxy could survive. POV: Zephyrine. Beat: the thematic crux; justice outside the law means choosing your verdict.

chapters.title: Gate of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Both fleets arrive at the jump gate as the Meridian Vale, flown by Brannoch, drifts into view between them — the ship both sides mourned, alive. Weapons arm. Zephyrine broadcasts on all channels, claiming the captain's authority via the manifest. POV: multiple. Beat: climax ignition; the ghost stands between armies.

chapters.title: The Verdict of One
chapters.summary: Facing mutual targeting locks, Zephyrine must broadcast either the exoneration (war) or the confession (peace at her mother's name). She splices them: the logs proving neither fleet guilty, and Ilsa's own voice explaining her sacrifice — truth enough to shame both fleets into standdown, incomplete enough to deny them a villain. POV: Zephyrine. Beat: climax resolution; the lie transformed into testimony.

chapters.title: Standdown
chapters.summary: Shamed by a dead woman's honesty, both fleet commanders accept joint custody of the Meridian Vale as a memorial. Sefa and Toma, enemies an hour ago, stand watch together. The jump window opens onto a lane reopening for the first time in a decade. POV: Sefa. Beat: catharsis; grief given somewhere to go.

chapters.title: What Inheritance Weighs
chapters.summary: Zephyrine files a final report with Halcyon Mutual closing the impossible claim: cause of loss, deliberate; beneficiary, everyone. She visits the restored ship where Ilsa's cabin bears a plaque bearing her true name at last. POV: Zephyrine. Beat: mourning completed; the daughter makes peace with the mother's choice.

chapters.title: Echo
chapters.summary: Months later, Zephyrine takes independent cases along the reopened routes, Toma navigating, Brannoch's engine humming beneath them. A new client brings an impossible manifest — and Zephyrine smiles, because some inheritances are meant to be carried forward. POV: Zephyrine. Beat: resolution with forward motion; the echo continues.
